title: Arancini
subtitle: Sicilian fried risotto balls with mozzarella
excerpt: Sicily's beloved fried rice balls: cold risotto shaped around a cube of mozzarella, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until golden and crunchy outside with a stretchy, molten cheese centre.

recipe.sourceNotes: Arancini (singular: arancino) are fried rice balls from Sicily, one of the most iconic of all Italian street foods. The name means 'little oranges', describing their size and shape. They are made from cold cooked risotto (saffron-flavoured for the plain version, or mixed with a ragù for the Catanese version), shaped into balls around a filling of mozzarella or meat ragù, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried. Arancini are a classic use of leftover risotto; a batch of risotto made specifically for arancini should be slightly firmer than usual so it holds its shape during shaping and frying. The mozzarella centre must be fior di latte (fresh cow's milk) or low-moisture mozzarella; fresh buffalo mozzarella is too wet and will not melt properly.

content.text: The risotto must be completely cold before shaping; warm rice will not hold together. Chill it for at least 2 hours or overnight. Press the rice firmly around the filling to compact it, then coat in breadcrumbs twice (double-breading) for a thicker, more protective crust that holds the cheese inside.

items.preparation: bloomed in a little warm water

content.text: Make the risotto: soften the onion in butter and oil. Add the rice and fry for 1 minute. Add the wine and let it absorb. Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring, until absorbed and the rice is cooked. Stir in the saffron water and Parmesan. Season. Spread onto a tray and cool completely; refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Scoop about 60 g of cold risotto into your palm. Press a cube of mozzarella into the centre and close the rice around it, rolling into a compact ball. Coat in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating for a double layer. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 175°C. Fry the arancini in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Eat immediately, while the mozzarella is still molten.
